attributes.residual: real 462, count-exact 843/843, 170 regnorm RENAMING rows plus the five OUTER clamp guards still unfused. Remaining --ops signature after the retained edit: target-only +10 b +5 bge +1 ble against ours-only -1 bgt -5 blt -10 fmr, i.e. two surplus `fmr` per clamp group in ours against two surplus `b` per group in the target. TWO BOUNDARY FINDINGS WORTH THE RECORD. (1) The IT law's front-end elision of an empty conditional body EXTENDS to the if/else-with-empty-THEN case: MWCC simply inverts `if (c) { } else { BODY }` to the single merged branch, so the empty-then form is a null for producing a forward branch pair even when an else is present and the statement therefore cannot be discarded whole. The IT law's measurements were all on `if (c) { }` with no else; this closes the remaining sub-case. (2) The outer guard is NOT reachable by the ternary carrier at acceptable cost here: the carrier does converge the branch architecture exactly as the IH law predicts (multiset 32t -> 20t, the largest structural gain measured this session) but it adds four instructions and costs half a fuzzy point. Because this function's realistic route to EXACT is the WebFrank recolor path - 170 renaming rows and only 15 genuine structural rows - count parity is worth more than the multiset gain, and the outer axis should be reopened only together with a lever for the two surplus per-group `fmr` copies.
